Stamp Duty Australia 2026: What You Pay in Every State and Territory

Published: 2 May 2026 · Last updated: 5 June 2026 · By Sarah Mitchell, CFA

Buying a property in Australia comes with one cost that surprises almost every first-time buyer: stamp duty. It is not hidden, but it is large — and because it is paid upfront at settlement, it can derail even the most carefully planned purchase budget. Stamp duty typically adds $15,000 to $50,000 on top of the purchase price for a median-priced property, depending on the state and the buyer's circumstances.

This guide covers stamp duty across all eight Australian states and territories in 2026. You will find out exactly how it is calculated, what you will pay at common purchase prices, and which concessions can legitimately reduce or eliminate your bill — particularly if you are a first home buyer.

Before you read on, use CalcPhi's free Stamp Duty Calculator to get an instant, state-specific figure for your property. It covers all eight jurisdictions, first home buyer concessions, and foreign buyer surcharges — no sign-up needed.

What Is Stamp Duty and How Does It Work?

Stamp duty — officially called transfer duty or conveyance duty in most states — is a state and territory government tax charged every time ownership of real estate changes hands. The buyer pays it, not the seller. It is calculated on the property's purchase price or market value, whichever is higher, using a tiered progressive structure similar to income tax brackets. That means only the portion of the price within each bracket is taxed at that bracket's rate, not the full purchase price.

Payment is typically required within 30 days of settlement. Miss that deadline and you can face interest charges and penalties from your state revenue office.

Because each state and territory runs its own stamp duty regime independently, rates, thresholds, and exemptions vary enormously across the country. Victoria currently has the highest top-bracket rate in Australia; Queensland is generally the most affordable for mid-range properties. Understanding these differences matters — especially if you are deciding between markets or comparing the true upfront cost of buying interstate.

New South Wales

New South Wales applies a progressive transfer duty scale. The first $14,000 of value is taxed at 1.25%, the scale continues progressively up to 7% for the portion above $3,000,000 (the premium property duty threshold).

Purchase Price Standard Duty (approx.)
$500,000$17,990
$750,000$29,240
$900,000$35,835
$1,000,000$39,412
$1,500,000$64,412

NSW first home buyers receive a full stamp duty exemption on homes (new or established) valued up to $800,000, with a sliding concession applying between $800,000 and $1,000,000. Above $1,000,000, full duty applies regardless of buyer status.

NSW also offers the First Home Buyer Choice scheme, which allows eligible buyers to opt for an annual property tax instead of lump-sum transfer duty at settlement. This can meaningfully reduce the upfront cash needed to buy. If you are buying in Sydney, use CalcPhi's First Home Buyer Calculator to model both options side by side.

Victoria

Victoria has the highest top-bracket stamp duty rate of any Australian state. Rates step up across five brackets from nil under $25,000 to 6.5% on the portion above $870,000 — the highest top-bracket rate in any Australian state.

Purchase Price Standard Duty (approx.)
$500,000$21,970
$700,000$37,070
$900,000$49,070
$1,000,000$55,000
$1,500,000$87,500

Victorian first home buyers pay no stamp duty on properties valued up to $600,000, with a partial concession for properties between $600,001 and $750,000. Above $750,000, full rates apply.

Victoria also offers an off-the-plan concession: when buying an apartment off the plan, stamp duty is calculated on the land value only at the contract date rather than the full completed property value. This concession has been extended and eligible apartments see significantly reduced duty calculated on land value only.

If you are weighing up renting versus buying in Melbourne, CalcPhi's Rent vs Buy Calculator factors stamp duty into the full upfront cost comparison.

Queensland

Queensland is generally the most affordable state for stamp duty on mid-range properties. The standard transfer duty scale starts at 1% for the first $5,000 and rises to 5.75% for the portion above $1,000,000. Stamp duty on a $600,000 property in QLD is approximately $15,925, compared to $22,490 in NSW and $31,070 in Victoria.

Purchase Price Standard Duty (approx.)
$500,000$15,925
$600,000$21,850
$750,000$27,600
$900,000$37,350
$1,000,000$38,025

Queensland's home concession rate applies when you purchase your principal place of residence and move in within 12 months, reducing the effective rate for owner-occupiers. For first home buyers, there is a full rebate on established homes up to $700,000 and zero stamp duty on new builds with no price cap — making it one of the most generous new-build concessions in the country. Queensland also offers a $30,000 First Home Owner Grant for new homes under $750,000, which can be stacked on top of the duty savings.

Western Australia

Western Australia uses a sliding transfer duty scale with the lowest top marginal stamp duty rate in Australia at 5.15%, with the scale starting at 1.9% for lower-value properties.

Purchase Price Standard Duty (approx.)
$400,000$11,115
$500,000$17,765
$700,000$26,740
$900,000$37,840

WA provides a transfer duty exemption for first home buyers on purchases up to $430,000, with concessions available up to $530,000. Perth's median house price has hit record highs as interstate migration continues — meaning most metropolitan suburbs now trade above the FHB threshold, and many first home buyers no longer qualify for the full exemption.

South Australia

South Australia charges stamp duty on a sliding scale from 1% to 5.5%, placing it broadly in the mid-range nationally. On a $600,000 SA property, standard duty is approximately $26,830.

The standout provision for first home buyers is that, since June 2024, first home buyers purchasing a new home in SA pay zero stamp duty with no price cap — a policy that significantly reduces the cost of entering the property market through a new build.

Tasmania

Tasmania applies transfer duty at progressive rates. Tasmania offers a full stamp duty exemption for first home buyers purchasing any property (new or established) valued up to $750,000, extended through to June 2026. A 50% duty discount also applies for all owner-occupied purchases up to $750,000, giving even non-first home buyers meaningful savings.

Foreign buyers in Tasmania pay an 8% surcharge on top of standard duty rates.

Australian Capital Territory

The ACT operates the most structurally different stamp duty regime in Australia. The ACT uses a sliding scale with rates from 0% to 4.95% and has been transitioning to a land tax model, gradually replacing stamp duty for owner-occupiers. Standard duty on a $600,000 ACT property is approximately $20,450.

First home buyers in the ACT can access a full stamp duty exemption through the Home Buyer Concession Scheme (HBCS) on properties up to $607,500, subject to an income test ($170,000 for singles, $227,000 for couples). The ACT also allows buyers to opt into an annual land tax payment in lieu of upfront duty — a mechanism it has offered longer than any other Australian jurisdiction.

Northern Territory

The Northern Territory applies transfer duty on a progressive scale, with amounts generally lower than southern states at equivalent property values. Standard duty on a $500,000 NT property is approximately $19,700.

The NT provides a First Home Owner Discount that reduces stamp duty by up to $18,601 on eligible purchases, alongside a Principal Place of Residence rebate. House-and-land package concessions in the NT apply until June 2027. The NT and ACT are the only two Australian jurisdictions that do not impose a foreign buyer stamp duty surcharge.

Foreign Buyer Surcharges

If you are not an Australian citizen or permanent resident, you pay an additional surcharge on top of standard stamp duty. As of May 2026, surcharge rates are 9% in NSW, 8% in Victoria, 8% in Queensland, 8% in Tasmania, 7% in Western Australia, and 7% in South Australia. The ACT and NT charge no foreign buyer surcharge.

On a $900,000 property in NSW, the surcharge alone is $81,000 — on top of the base stamp duty of approximately $35,835, bringing the total to roughly $116,835. Temporary visa holders, including those on 482 and student visas, are generally treated as foreign persons for stamp duty purposes.

Worked Example: What Does Stamp Duty Actually Cost?

To make these numbers concrete, here is a real-world scenario comparing two buyers — Sarah and Marcus — who are purchasing at the same price in different states.

Sarah — First Home Buyer in New South Wales ($780,000 Purchase)

Sarah is buying her first home in Newcastle for $780,000. Because this is below NSW's $800,000 first home buyer exemption threshold, she pays zero stamp duty. Without the exemption, the standard duty on a $780,000 NSW property would be approximately $30,068. Sarah saves that entire amount by qualifying under the First Home Buyers Assistance Scheme.

Sarah still needs to budget for other upfront costs — conveyancing, building inspection, and potentially Lenders Mortgage Insurance (LMI) if her deposit is under 20%. Use CalcPhi's LMI Calculator to estimate that cost and plan your full deposit strategy.

Marcus — Owner-Occupier in Victoria ($780,000 Purchase)

Marcus is buying his second home in Geelong for $780,000 and does not qualify for any first home buyer concession. Under Victoria's rate schedule, he pays the full standard duty. Using Victoria's progressive brackets — nil under $25,000, stepping up to 6.5% on the portion above $870,000 — Marcus's duty on $780,000 works out to approximately $41,740. That is over $41,000 more than Sarah pays for a property at the same price, purely because of the state and buyer status difference.

Marcus budgets for this before taking out his mortgage. To see how stamp duty affects total borrowing capacity and monthly repayments, use CalcPhi's Mortgage Calculator and Borrowing Power Calculator together.

The key takeaway

The same $780,000 purchase results in a stamp duty bill of $0 in NSW (for a first home buyer) versus approximately $41,740 in Victoria (for a standard buyer). State of purchase and buyer status are the two most powerful variables in any stamp duty calculation. Always model your specific scenario before committing to a purchase — run your numbers in seconds with CalcPhi's free Stamp Duty Calculator.

How to Reduce Your Stamp Duty Legally

Stamp duty is not fixed — there are several legitimate strategies to reduce or eliminate it depending on your circumstances.

The most straightforward path is buying as a first home buyer below your state's exemption threshold. In NSW, that means staying under $800,000; in Victoria, under $600,000; in Queensland, under $700,000 for established homes (or building new with no price cap). If you are close to a threshold, a $10,000 reduction in the purchase price could save $20,000 or more in duty if it keeps you inside the exemption bracket.

Buying a new build in South Australia or Queensland as a first home buyer avoids stamp duty entirely regardless of price. In Victoria, purchasing off the plan significantly reduces the duty base by limiting it to land value. In the ACT, opting for the annual land tax model instead of upfront duty reduces the immediate cash needed at settlement. Pensioner concessions exist in several states for eligible downsizers.

Frequently Asked Questions

  • How is stamp duty calculated in Australia?

    Stamp duty is calculated using a tiered bracket system applied to the property's purchase price or market value, whichever is higher. Only the portion of value within each bracket is taxed at that bracket's rate — similar to how income tax brackets work. The total duty is the sum of tax applied across all applicable brackets. Rates and bracket thresholds are set separately by each state and territory government and differ considerably across jurisdictions.

  • Which Australian state has the lowest stamp duty?

    Queensland generally has the lowest stamp duty for mid-range properties. Stamp duty on a $600,000 property is approximately $15,925 in QLD, compared to $22,490 in NSW and $31,070 in VIC. For higher-value purchases, WA is often the cheapest thanks to its top marginal rate of just 5.15% — the lowest in the country.

  • Do first home buyers pay stamp duty in Australia?

    Most first home buyers pay reduced or zero stamp duty in 2026. Full exemptions apply up to $800,000 in NSW, $600,000 in Victoria, and $700,000 for established homes in Queensland — with no price cap at all on new builds in QLD and SA. Thresholds, income tests, and eligibility conditions vary by state, so always confirm your entitlement with the relevant state revenue office before committing to a purchase.

  • When is stamp duty paid in Australia?

    Stamp duty is due within 30 days of settlement in most states and territories. Your conveyancer or solicitor calculates the amount and coordinates payment as part of the settlement process. Late payment can attract interest and penalties from the relevant state revenue authority. In NSW and the ACT, eligible buyers may be able to opt for an annual land tax in lieu of a lump-sum payment at settlement.

  • What is the foreign buyer stamp duty surcharge in Australia?

    Foreign buyers pay an additional surcharge on top of standard stamp duty when purchasing residential property in Australia. As of May 2026, surcharge rates are 9% in NSW, 8% in Victoria, Queensland, and Tasmania, and 7% in Western Australia and South Australia. The ACT and NT are the only jurisdictions with no foreign buyer surcharge. Temporary visa holders — including those on 482, student, and other temporary visas — are generally treated as foreign persons for duty purposes.

  • Is stamp duty tax-deductible in Australia?

    Stamp duty on a principal place of residence is not tax-deductible. For investment properties, however, it forms part of the property's cost base and can reduce your capital gains tax liability when you eventually sell — it raises the base cost, which reduces the taxable gain at disposal. It cannot be immediately deducted against rental income in the year of purchase. Always confirm your specific position with a registered tax agent. For a clearer picture of CGT exposure on an investment property, use CalcPhi's Capital Gains Tax Calculator.

  • Can stamp duty be added to a home loan in Australia?

    Stamp duty cannot generally be added directly to your mortgage in Australia. Lenders require it to be paid as an upfront cost at settlement from your own funds. In most states, it must be settled within 30 days of the property transaction completing. This makes it a critical item to save for separately alongside your deposit. Some lenders may factor it into their overall assessment of your liquid savings when evaluating your loan application, which is another reason to budget for it well in advance.
